title: Every reference to every Objective-C ivar offset cell in the pinned ELF
mechanism: ivar offset cell reached via a .got entry whose file contents are the cell VA
method: OBJC_IVAR_$_C.i denotes a 4-byte cell in __objc_ivar; code reaches it through a two-word PIC idiom whose middle address is a .got entry, and *that entry's file contents are the cell VA*. A reference exists exactly when *(wA + v) is a known cell VA, v being the PIC base 0x105faf4.

counts.note: a 24-instruction bias window resolves only 13430/27155 add sites and understated every number here by ~34%; 240 resolves 20593 and changed neither field's site list

World.worldTime.property: not present in the property table; getter -[World worldTime] only, NO setter in the method table
World.worldTime.conclusion: three references, ALL reads (weather getter, World render:, own getter) - the 20-units-per-second clock is not advanced by any ivar store in this library

World.fastForward.property: DECLARED READONLY PROPERTY: attributes 'Tc,R,VfastForward' in the property table; no setter exists
World.fastForward.conclusion: exactly one reference, the byte read in its own getter. No writer, no setter (readonly property), and no overlapping neighbour: 934 is a standalone char between 933 idleTimerDisabled and 936 saveCount. Nothing outside libApplication names the field either - no other .so in the APK contains the string

literal_offset_half.what: the complement sweep: stores with a literal offset #0x288 (648) / #0x3a6 (934) in the code window
literal_offset_half.result: no World-object field store: the hits are stack slots ([sp, #0x648] / [sp, #0x3a4]) or draw-buffer offsets - dozens of -draw: methods write a vertex buffer at 0x648, which is why a naive literal sweep looks alarming and means nothing
literal_offset_half.conclusion: neither field is written by a cell-based OR a literal-offset store

boundary: The access classification is heuristic: it reads the instruction sequence after the site. It was hand-verified against four known sites (the worldTime getter, two worldTime reads, the fastForward getter) and four earlier classification bugs were found by the self-check.
The scan resolves 20593 of 27155 add-sites; the ~6500 unresolved ones are not claimed covered.

Absence of a write is a statement about this library. A runtime-resolved offset (KVC setValue:forKey: / object_setIvar with the ivar fetched by name), a table-indexed offset write, or a bulk copy into the object are all still open.

Method attribution is reported with its basis: unique / ambiguous / none, plus every method-table entry in [fn_start, site]. The fastForward site is 'ambiguous' on purpose - it sits in a run of one-line getters sharing one body.

Method naming is weaker than the cell fact for the shared one-line-getter body (the tool reports attribution 'ambiguous' there): read fastForward's single row as one cell-resolving site inside that body, not as 'its own getter'.
